questions.question: What single question does the verification gate answer?
options: Is the current prompt template the optimal one for this particular class of task?
Is the model's response fast enough to keep the agent loop under its latency budget?
Is this task actually complete? answered by reading scope, rule, feedback, and diff artifacts
Is the token budget for this whole session still healthy enough to finish all of the remaining work?
questions.explanation: The gate is a deterministic function over workbench artifacts producing a pass/fail verdict.

questions.question: Why must the gate be deterministic?
options: The same artifact set must produce the same verdict every time; LLM judges belong in the reviewer, not the gate
Determinism is required because the hosting provider bills extra for every nondeterministic call the gate ever makes
A probabilistic gate would need a much larger context window than the workbench currently budgets for
Nondeterministic gates cannot be represented at all inside the verification_report.json schema
questions.explanation: Mixing model judgment into the gate collapses the deterministic/qualitative split.

questions.question: What is the gate's override discipline?
options: Any team member can silently override a block finding as long as the merge succeeds afterward
Only a human can override a block finding, with a recorded override_reason and overridden_by id
The agent itself can override a block finding once it re-runs the failing acceptance command a second time
Overrides require only a manager's email address forwarded into the pull request thread
questions.explanation: Signed overrides land in outputs/verification/overrides.jsonl; agent cannot self-override.

questions.question: What is the Hybrid Norm pairing the lesson cites?
options: Verifiable rewards like tests and exit codes answer whether it solved the problem; rubrics judge style
Hot prompts run on GPUs while cold prompts fall back to CPU inference for the same request
One pass checks correctness twice; a second identical pass just confirms the first pass was not a fluke
The gate caches results while the reviewer always runs a fresh, uncached pass over the diff
questions.explanation: Anthropic 2026 guidance: gate runs the first class; reviewer (Lesson 39) runs the second.

questions.question: How does defense-in-depth layer the gates?
options: Single gate at merge time
Pre-commit hook -> CI status check -> pre-tool authz hook -> pre-merge gate; each layer is deterministic so failure in one is caught by the next
Only IDE warnings
Only a chat reminder
questions.explanation: Multiple non-bypassable layers catch what a single layer would miss.

questions.question: What does a coverage_floor check protect against?
options: Cold starts on the CI runner, a cost the gate has no way to measure from the artifacts it is given to read
Agents quietly deleting failing tests; the gate blocks if coverage drops below the floor or regresses
Outdated lockfiles, which the gate flags separately from any coverage-related finding
Hot-path latency, which the coverage_floor check reports as a warn-severity finding
questions.explanation: Without a floor, agents can silently lower coverage to keep the verdict green.

questions.question: When should --strict mode promote every warn to block?
options: Always, since --strict is meant to be the permanent default posture for every branch
Never, since promoting warnings to blocks would make the gate impossible to pass
Release branches, ship-blocking PRs, and post-incident triage, not the daily default
Only on branches whose name matches a regex configured in the gate's own settings file
questions.explanation: --strict is opt-in by branch; reserve for high-stakes moments.
